topic: Bitten by a snake: suck the venom out or keep still?
title: Bitten By A Snake
idea: Sucking out venom pulls out almost nothing; keeping still and getting to a hospital is what works.
hook: A snake just bit your hand. Suck it out, or keep still?

beats.see: Close on the hand: two fang dots, the fingers puff up like balloons around a ring. Hits on 'swell'.

beats.line: In the movies, someone always sucks the venom out.
beats.see: Cardboard film frame with a clapperboard snap; a cutout hero bends over the bite. Clapper on 'movies', card A glows on 'sucks'.

beats.line: In a lab test, suction got out less than one percent.
beats.see: A tiny suction cup on a model arm, a beaker fills with a single drop; big counter '<1%' stamps on 'percent', card A gets a red X.

beats.line: Snakebites kill up to one hundred thirty eight thousand people a year.
beats.see: Counter rolls up to 138,000 over a world map made of paper dots. Number lands on 'thousand'.

beats.line: Keep still wins. Moving pushes venom through your lymph.
beats.see: Card B gets a green check on 'wins'; x-ray view of the arm: a glowing lymph network, the hero wiggles and a purple stain races up the lines on 'Moving', freezes when he stops.

beats.line: One. Take off rings and watches before the swelling traps them.
beats.see: Step card 1 RINGS OFF; ring and watch slide off on 'Take', the finger swells right after on 'traps'.

beats.line: Two. Rest the arm in a comfy position and keep it still.
beats.see: Step card 2 KEEP STILL; arm settles on a pillow in a cardboard splint on 'Rest', a padlock icon clicks on 'still'.

beats.line: Three. Let someone drive you to a hospital for antivenom.
beats.see: Step card 3 HOSPITAL; hero in the passenger seat, a friend drives, hospital sign and an antivenom vial pop on 'antivenom'.

end.line: Picked suck it out? Replay it and keep still this time.
end.see: Cards A and B return big; A slides off on 'Picked', the clip rewinds to the bite on 'Replay', card B pulses on 'still'.

description: Bitten by a snake: suck the venom out or keep still? The movie move gets almost none of it.

facts.claim: Swelling follows a venomous bite; remove rings and watches before swelling starts.
Do not suck out venom (or cut, tourniquet, ice).
Suction removed about 0.04 % of mock venom in a human model, i.e. less than one percent.
facts.source: Alberts et al., Ann Emerg Med 2004, PubMed 14747805

facts.claim: Snakebite kills 81,410 to 137,880 people a year (up to 138,000).
Venom mainly spreads through the lymph system, which is why moving spreads it; keep calm and still, immobilize the limb.
Keep the limb in a neutral position of comfort, immobilized/splinted.
Get emergency care; antivenom is the effective treatment; do not drive yourself.

notes: Correct card: B (KEEP STILL). Card A text 'SUCK IT' to keep 2 words (alt: 'SUCK OUT'). The 'less than one percent' comes from a mock-venom human model study seen only as snippet; FACTS allows this wording. Lab test = model, not real patients; line says 'lab test' to stay honest. 'In the movies' is a pop-culture framing, not a factual claim. No 'below the heart', no tight bandage, no spread-speed number.
